dedupe_keys.name: ghana gis based energy system modelling of solar mini grids for health facilities and their communities

description: This case study identifies which health facilities in Ghana are suited to electrification with photovoltaic mini-grids to make their services more reliable and energy self-sufficient. The authors, from German research institutes working on energy access, published it as an open-access journal article. They classified health facilities by access to electricity, identified settlements within each facility's catchment, estimated electricity demand for facilities and surrounding communities, and used GIS-based energy system modelling to choose mini-grid set-ups and estimate the accumulated solar mini-grid potential for all suitable sites. Coverage is Ghana. The article is free under a Creative Commons Attribution licence. Caveats: demand estimates depend on assumed facility and household loads, facility inventories and grid status data may be incomplete, and findings should not be transferred between facility types. The study concludes that solar mini-grids are a promising way to electrify health facilities, that including community demand balances and stabilises the energy system, and that health and energy planning should be integrated. Simulation uses: a template for coupling healthcare facility inventories with energy system models for resilience and investment appraisal. Related records: the sub-Saharan Africa health facility PV study (case_study-sub-saharan-africa-health-facility-pv-electrification) and the sub-Saharan public health facilities list (data-ssa-public-health-facilities) are related.
